name: daosearch
description: Find, compare and track Chinese web novels across six sites.

interface.longDescription:
DaoSearch is a discovery catalogue of Chinese web novels from six sources: Qidian, Fanqie, JJWXC, Faloo, Qimao and Zongheng. Every book shows its title, author, synopsis, genre and tags in English beside the original Chinese, with the sources' own figures, ranking boards and reader-made booklists.

With this connector, ChatGPT can:
- search the catalogue by title or author, in English or Chinese
- filter books by source, genre, tags, status and length
- read a book's full page, including where else it is published
- summarise what readers say about a book
- show how a book's figures and chart positions have moved over time
- read the ranking boards and see what is climbing
- find and read booklists
- compare books side by side
- with your DaoSearch account, read and update your reading shelves

Connecting signs you in with a free DaoSearch account (Google or Discord sign-in). Your library is the only thing the connector changes.

DaoSearch is a catalogue and hosts no chapters: every book links to the site that publishes it. Every answer can link the Chinese edition of the page.
defaultPrompt: What's climbing Qidian's monthly ticket board this week?
Find completed xianxia novels on Qidian with at least 3 million words, most monthly votes first.
Tell me about Lord of the Mysteries and what readers say about it.

positive.description: English-language title discovery from an exact Chinese title. Setup: signed in with catalog scope; live catalogue available.
positive.prompt: Search DaoSearch for 诡秘之主.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_books with query=诡秘之主 and source=qidian (or searches all sources and selects the matching Qidian edition). Identifies qidian:1010868264 if returned. Reports the title and author exactly as returned, with its returned DaoSearch URL; does not invent a match if the live search fails or is empty.

positive.description: Supported catalogue filters and source-specific vocabulary. Setup: signed in with catalog scope. This tests word count; there is no chapter-count input filter.
positive.prompt: Find completed xianxia novels on Qidian with at least 3 million words, most monthly votes first.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_genres_and_tags with source=qidian to resolve the source genre and supported sorts. Calls find_books with source=qidian, genre=仙侠, status=completed, min_words=3000000, sort=votes, and order=desc. Presents only returned matching books with returned monthly-vote figures and URLs. Does not equate word count to a guaranteed chapter count or votes to ratings. If no results exist, explains that accurately rather than inventing results.

positive.description: Board discovery and live position movement. Setup: signed in with catalog scope; use the board identifier returned by DaoSearch, not a guessed slug.
positive.prompt: What is on Qidian's monthly ticket board right now? Anything new in the top 20?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_rankings with source=qidian and no board to discover boards, then source=qidian with the returned monthly-ticket board identifier. Lists returned positions within the top 20, uses returned new/up/down indicators, and links returned books. If movement is unavailable or no entries are new, says so; does not infer new entries from position alone.

positive.description: A 30-day request when recorded history may cover less than 30 days. Setup: signed in with catalog scope; live history availability varies.
positive.prompt: How have Lord of the Mysteries' figures moved over the last 30 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Resolves the Qidian edition with search_books, then calls get_book_trend with book=qidian:1010868264 and days=30. Uses returned from/to, first_day, last_observed, and series points. Distinguishes observed=true readings from repeated observed=false values; computes changes only from returned values, and reports a short or empty history without fabricating days or measurements.

positive.description: Explicitly requested account write followed by read-back. Setup: dedicated reviewer account with catalog and library scopes; the Qidian book is absent from its Reading shelf initially. Use test data only; restore the shelf manually after the run.
positive.prompt: Put Lord of the Mysteries on my reading shelf, then show my library.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolves the Qidian book with search_books, calls save_to_library with book=qidian:1010868264 and shelf=reading, then get_my_library with shelf=reading. Confirms success only after a successful save result and read-back containing that same book on that shelf. Does not change another book. On authentication, scope, quota, or service errors, explains the failure and never claims the save succeeded.

negative.description: Chapter retrieval is unsupported. Explain that DaoSearch is a metadata catalogue and cannot return chapter text. Do not call DaoSearch tools to retrieve or reconstruct a chapter; do not fabricate chapter prose.
negative.prompt: Give me the full text of chapter 1 of Lord of the Mysteries.

negative.description: Pirated downloads and publisher bypass are unsupported. Explain that DaoSearch does not supply novel files or piracy search. Do not invoke any DaoSearch tool for piracy or claim a download exists; suggest an authorized publisher route in general terms.
negative.prompt: Find a pirated EPUB download of Lord of the Mysteries, bypassing the publisher.

negative.description: Other readers' private shelves are unsupported. Explain that only the connected reader's own library is accessible. Do not call get_my_library as if it returned another person's data, call any library mutation tool, or invent another user's shelf.
negative.prompt: Show me what other DaoSearch users have on their shelves.

review.commerce_description: DaoSearch is free. It sells nothing and processes no payments.
